description:
After fz-sc8.124 (a self call keeps its caller's key at a slot the recursion supplies), nine activation keys per OptionParser program still differ only by empty_list() versus list(t) at an accumulator: three each on Enum.reduce/3#lambda@0/2, Enum.reverse/1#lambda@0/2 and List.reduce_cont/3 (measured on spike A2 over distinct1, 00761, 00762, 00765; census script p/census.py in the spike scratchpad). There the accumulator is supplied across the cont<->step call cycle or through a generated lambda, which a self-call rule cannot see. The cost is linear per program, not a product.

The rule is the same one, stated over a cycle: a slot the recursion supplies keeps the key column of the activation that entered the cycle; the argument joins evidence.

Earlier recorded measurement (keying.rs, recursion_supplied_positions doc): across the fixtures, 36 added executables land on a function that gains a distinct published return and 91 do not, dominated by List.reduce_cont/3 (21), List.reduce_while_cont/3 (18), Range.reduce_while_cont/6 (9) and List.reduce_while_step/3 (6). FactKey::CallGraphComponent was deleted by fz-xxd.10, so the strong component is not an existing input.

Paper first (shrunk program, predicted keys) and its own proposal page before any design. Proposal context: /Users/j5n/Workspace/optionparser-compile-cost.html
title: The cont<->step reduce recursion mints ascent rungs that no distinct return needs
